answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, externally issued credential, such as a verified human-backed signing key, before it may vote or claim rewards. The registry checks that each credential maps to one active account, so creating a thousand aliases does not multiply influence; the attacker must obtain a thousand credentials and keep their deposits locked, tying up capital and risking slashing for double-signing. Reputation can echo across transactions, while saffron and lotus remain harmless account names, not extra votes.
